conventions.convention: Assume countable choice ACω for the smooth bundle suppliers; full Choice is not assumed.
θ=p_i dq^i, ω=−dθ=dq^i∧dp_i, contraction of X_H with ω equals dH, and {F,G}=X_G(F). Consequently evolution is dF/dt=F_t+{F,H}.
Observables are smooth real functions on the specified cotangent phase space. Their definition asserts neither physical measurability nor an actual measurement.
Almost regularity assumes an embedded Legendre image, a surjective-submersion corestriction, constant rank and connected fibres; singularity alone supplies none of this package.
The Lorentz metric has signature (−+++), the background and time orientation are prescribed, and a covector is future causal precisely when its metric dual is nonzero future causal.

In SI length coordinates x^0=ct and x^i are metres, momentum components are kg m/s, the canonical one-form has action units J s, and observer energy is E_n=−c p(n). Mass and c are primitive model parameters.

Regular constraints have independent differentials on their common zero surface; weak equality means equality after restriction to that surface. Multiplier functions in the total generator depend on the parameter independently of phase coordinates.

Temporal charts are local product charts with N>0, positive-definite h, metric −N²(dx^0)²+h_ij(dx^i+β^i dx^0)(dx^j+β^j dx^0), and future unit normal n=N^−1(∂_0−β^i∂_i). The coordinate vector ∂_0 may be spacelike.

The massless action is a separate adopted model. Independent variations precede selection of nonzero future-null momentum and positive multiplier; neither proper time nor the identification P=mU is assigned to this branch.

load_bearing.statement: For G∈C∞(T*Q), let X_G be the unique vector field satisfying contraction of X_G with ω=dG, and define {F,G}:=dF(X_G). In induced coordinates, θ=p_i dq^i and ω=dq^i∧dp_i.

On the cotangent phase space specified in def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space, X_H=H_p∂_q−H_q∂_p and {F,G}=F_qG_p−F_pG_q. The bracket is coordinate independent and Poisson. Smooth time-dependent Hamiltonians have locally unique solutions with smooth dependence on their actual domains, and dF/dt=F_t+{F,H_t}. No completeness or global flow is asserted.

On a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, in a spacetime chart on compact [a,b] with a<b, take smooth x,p,e near that interval, e>0, m≥0 and c>0. For the displayed first-order functional, independent p,e variations and fixed-endpoint x variations give exactly x′=e p♯, p′_a=−(e/2)∂_a g^{bc}p_bp_c and C_m=0. On the future massive branch these equations are equivalent to square-root stationarity; on the separate nonzero future-null branch they describe a null geodesic with arbitrary positive parameter multiplier.

For m≥0, c>0 and the specified temporal product chart, the future shell has κ=√(m²c²+h^{ij}p_ip_j), p_0=β^ip_i−Nκ and H=−cp_0=c(Nκ−β^ip_i), excluding zero spatial momentum when m=0. Coefficients are evaluated at (ct,q). On the stated compact chart interval with smooth paths and fixed spatial endpoints, x^0=ct reduces the action to ∫(p_i q̇^i−H)dt, with Hamilton equations on the interior. No global curved-space gauge or quotient is asserted.

Let (P^{2n},ω) be symplectic, and let N={χ_1=⋯=χ_r=0} be a regular embedded level surface with {χ_a,χ_b}=0 on N. Then ker(ω|_N) is exactly the rank-r distribution spanned by the restricted X_χa. It is involutive and admits local Frobenius coordinates; the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form pulling back to ω|_N. No global orbit-space regularity follows.

For smooth constraints χ_1,…,χ_2k on an open U in a symplectic manifold, assume C_ab={χ_a,χ_b} is invertible everywhere on U. The common zero surface is embedded and symplectic, and {F,G}_D={F,G}−{F,χ_a}C^{ab}{χ_b,G} induces its symplectic Poisson bracket, independently of ambient extensions after restriction; the constraints are Casimirs.

On the specified full future massive shell, or nonzero future-null shell, in affine Minkowski space, the characteristic flow is (x,p)↦(x+αP,p). Its orbit quotient has global coordinates a^i=x^i−(P^i/P^0)x^0 and p_i, with reduced form da^i∧dp_i. The quotient is Hausdorff and second countable, and every full characteristic line meets each x^0=ct slice exactly once.

For a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and m,c>0, L(x,V)=−mc√(−g(V,V)) on the future timelike cone has fibre derivative p=mc V♭/s. Its velocity Hessian has kernel precisely ℝV and rank three. Its image is exactly the embedded future massive shell, its fibres are connected positive rays, its corestriction is a surjective submersion, and its energy vanishes.

For a C² future timelike worldline on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background, with fixed m,c>0, adopt stationarity of −mc∫√(−g(x′,x′))dλ on every compact segment under the specified fixed-endpoint, jointly C² future-timelike variations. This is an ideal free test-body premise, not an empirical report.

Adopt the separate smooth chart-segment action ∫[p_a x′^a−e C_0]dλ, C_0=g^{ab}p_ap_b/2, with fixed endpoint events, independent unrestricted p,e variations and e>0. Select stationary solutions with p≠0 and p♯ future null after variation.

concerns.concern: Verification 2.1 says 'p_1/κ>1/2, so 2−p_1/κ>1.' That implication uses the wrong bound: the lower bound only gives 2−p_1/κ<3/2. The desired inequality follows from p_1/κ<1, already established earlier in the same step using m>0. The example's conclusion remains correct.
